```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
library(moderndive)
library(modelsummary)
library(infer)
library(countdown)

# Colors from _brand.yml
clrs <- list(
  blue = "#2878B5",
  orange = "#E17C05",
  gold = "#F2B701",
  maroon = "#8A1538",
  purple = "#6F4C9B",
  green = "#2D934F",
  gray = "#696A6F"
)

theme_set(theme_grey(base_size = 14))

# p-values that are 0 in a simulation really just mean "smaller than 1 in 1,000"
fmt_p <- \(p) case_when(
  p < 0.001 ~ "< 0.001",
  p > 0.999 ~ "≈ 1",
  .default = paste("=", format(round(p, 3), nsmall = 3))
)

# Same as fmt_p() but without the "=", for table cells
fmt_p_cell <- \(p) str_remove(fmt_p(p), "^= ")

# Null world histogram with the observed δ and two-sided p-value shading
plot_null <- function(null, obs, x_lab, labels = waiver()) {
  visualize(null) +
    shade_p_value(obs_stat = obs, direction = "two-sided", color = clrs$orange, fill = clrs$orange) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = labels) +
    labs(title = NULL, x = x_lab, y = "Count")
}

# Shared look for little tinytables
tt_nice <- \(x, size = 0.7) {
  x |>
    tt() |>
    style_tt(fontsize = size) |>
    theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: make-data
#| include: false

vdem <- readRDS(here::here("projects", "regression-inference", "data", "vdem.rds")) |>
  mutate(
    democracy = if_else(regime_num >= 2, "Democracy", "Autocracy"),
    gdp_1000 = gdpPercap / 1000
  )

barometer <- readRDS(here::here("projects", "regression-inference", "data", "barometer.rds"))

happiness <- read_csv(
  here::here("projects", "regression-inference", "data", "world_happiness.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  mutate(gdp_1000 = gdp_per_cap / 1000)

# Slopes are δs too: happiness and unemployment
happy_unemp <- happiness |> drop_na(unemployment_rate)
model_unemp <- lm(happiness ~ unemployment_rate, data = happy_unemp)
tidy_unemp <- broom::tidy(model_unemp, conf.int = TRUE)

obs_slope <- happy_unemp |>
  specify(happiness ~ unemployment_rate) |>
  calculate(stat = "slope")

set.seed(1234)
null_slope <- happy_unemp |>
  specify(happiness ~ unemployment_rate) |>
  hypothesize(null = "independence") |>
  generate(reps = 1000, type = "permute") |>
  calculate(stat = "slope")

p_slope_sim <- get_p_value(null_slope, obs_slope, direction = "two-sided")$p_value

# Three ways, means: life expectancy in democracies vs. autocracies
vdem_life <- vdem |> drop_na(life_exp)

obs_life <- vdem_life |>
  specify(life_exp ~ democracy) |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in means", order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"))

set.seed(1234)
null_life <- vdem_life |>
  specify(life_exp ~ democracy) |>
  hypothesize(null = "independence") |>
  generate(reps = 1000, type = "permute") |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in means", order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"))

p_life_sim <- suppressWarnings(get_p_value(null_life, obs_life, direction = "two-sided")$p_value)
t_life <- t_test(vdem_life, life_exp ~ democracy, order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"), var.equal = TRUE)
lm_life <- broom::tidy(lm(life_exp ~ democracy, data = vdem_life))

# Three ways, means: turnout in democracies vs. autocracies (not significant)
vdem_turnout <- vdem |> drop_na(turnout)

obs_turnout <- vdem_turnout |>
  specify(turnout ~ democracy) |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in means", order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"))

set.seed(1234)
null_turnout <- vdem_turnout |>
  specify(turnout ~ democracy) |>
  hypothesize(null = "independence") |>
  generate(reps = 1000, type = "permute") |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in means", order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"))

p_turnout_sim <- get_p_value(null_turnout, obs_turnout, direction = "two-sided")$p_value
t_turnout <- t_test(vdem_turnout, turnout ~ democracy, order = c("Democracy", "Autocracy"), var.equal = TRUE)
lm_turnout <- broom::tidy(lm(turnout ~ democracy, data = vdem_turnout))

# Three ways, proportions: voting by gender in Mauritania
mauritania <- barometer |>
  filter(country == "Mauritania") |>
  drop_na(voted, gender) |>
  mutate(voted_num = as.numeric(voted == "Yes"))

obs_vote <- mauritania |>
  specify(voted ~ gender, success = "Yes") |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in props", order = c("Female", "Male"))

set.seed(1234)
null_vote <- mauritania |>
  specify(voted ~ gender, success = "Yes") |>
  hypothesize(null = "independence") |>
  generate(reps = 1000, type = "permute") |>
  calculate(stat = "diff in props", order = c("Female", "Male"))

p_vote_sim <- get_p_value(null_vote, obs_vote, direction = "two-sided")$p_value
prop_vote <- prop_test(mauritania, voted ~ gender, success = "Yes", order = c("Female", "Male"), correct = FALSE)
lm_vote <- broom::tidy(lm(voted_num ~ gender, data = mauritania))

# Several groups: women legislators by regime type
vdem_women <- vdem |> drop_na(women_legislators)
model_regime <- lm(women_legislators ~ regime, data = vdem_women)
tidy_regime <- broom::tidy(model_regime)

regime_means <- vdem_women |>
  group_by(regime) |>
  summarize(
    avg = mean(women_legislators),
    se = sd(women_legislators) / sqrt(n()),
    n = n()
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lower = avg - qt(0.975, n - 1) * se,
    upper = avg + qt(0.975, n - 1) * se
  )

# Side-by-side table: women legislators, wealth, and democracy
vdem_wl <- vdem |> drop_na(women_legislators, gdp_1000, polyarchy)
model_wl_1 <- lm(women_legislators ~ gdp_1000, data = vdem_wl)
model_wl_2 <- lm(women_legislators ~ polyarchy, data = vdem_wl)
model_wl_3 <- lm(women_legislators ~ gdp_1000 + polyarchy, data = vdem_wl)

wl_models <- list("(1)" = model_wl_1, "(2)" = model_wl_2, "(3)" = model_wl_3)
wl_coefs <- c(
  "gdp_1000" = "GDP per capita",
  "polyarchy" = "Democracy",
  "(Intercept)" = "Constant"
)

b_wl_1 <- broom::tidy(model_wl_1) |> filter(term == "gdp_1000")
b_wl_3 <- broom::tidy(model_wl_3) |> filter(term == "gdp_1000")
```

## Slopes are δs too {.clr-1}

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

model <- lm(happiness ~ unemployment_rate, data = happiness)
get_regression_table(model)
```
:::

```{r}
get_regression_table(model_unemp) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.7) |>
  style_tt(i = 2, j = 2:5, background = "#f7e896", bold = TRUE) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

::: {.incremental .small .sp-before}
- Same δ: `r round(tidy_unemp$estimate[2], 3)`
- Basically the same p-value: `r round(tidy_unemp$p.value[2], 3)` (math) vs. `r round(p_slope_sim, 3)` (simulation)
- Every row in a regression table is a hypothesis test with $H_0: \beta = 0$
:::

## {.clr-1}

```{r}
get_regression_table(model_unemp) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.6) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

::: {.list-table widths="1,4" .smaller .sp-before-half}

- - Column
  - What it means

- - `estimate`
  - δ (or β): the slope or the difference between groups

- - `std_error`
  - How much the estimate would bounce around from sample to sample

- - `statistic`
  - `estimate / std_error`: how many standard errors δ is away from 0 (a *t* statistic)

- - `p_value`
  - In a world where β is 0ish, the probability of seeing something at least this extreme

- - `lower_ci`, `upper_ci`
  - The 95% confidence interval for β

:::

## Kinda cheating, rough shortcuts {.clr-1}

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
[If `statistic` is bigger than ≈2 (or smaller than ≈−2), p < 0.05]{.box-clr-1-light}
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
[If the 95% confidence interval doesn't include 0, p < 0.05]{.box-clr-1-light}
:::
::::

:::::

::: {.sp-before}
[Both mean the same thing!]{.box-clr-1 .small .fragment}

[δ is far enough away from 0 that it'd be weird in the null world]{.box-clr-1 .small .fragment}
:::

## Templates {.clr-1}

::: {.list-table widths="1,3,3,3" .smaller}

- - X
  - β
  - p < α
  - p ≥ α

- - Continuous
  - On average, a one-unit increase in **X** is associated with a **β** change in **Y** (**confidence interval**).
  - This is statistically significant (p = **BLAH**), so we are confident that it's not zero and that there is a relationship.
  - However, this is not statistically significant (p = **BLAH**), so we cannot rule out the possibility that the true relationship is zero.

- - Categorical
  - On average, **Y** is **β** higher (or lower) in this group (**confidence interval**), compared to **the base case**.
  - This is statistically significant (p = **BLAH**), so we are confident that it's not zero and that there is a difference.
  - However, this is not statistically significant (p = **BLAH**), so we cannot rule out the possibility that the true difference is zero.
:::

## {.clr-1}

```{r}
get_regression_table(model_unemp) |>
  tt() |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.7) |>
  style_tt(i = 2, background = "#f7e896", bold = TRUE) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

::: {.fragment .sp-before}
[On average, a 1 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate is associated with a `r abs(round(tidy_unemp$estimate[2], 3))`-point decrease in happiness (95% CI: [`r round(tidy_unemp$conf.low[2], 3)`, `r round(tidy_unemp$conf.high[2], 3)`]). This is statistically significant (p `r fmt_p(tidy_unemp$p.value[2])`), so we are confident that it's not zero and that there is a relationship.]{.box-clr-1-light .small}
:::

::: {.fragment .small .sp-before}
Is that big? Happiness is on a 0–10 scale, and going from 5% to 15% unemployment would mean happiness drops by about half a point
:::

# Everything<br>is regression {background-color="{{< brand color clr-5 >}}" background-image="/slides/img/background-hex-shapes.svg" background-opacity="0.25"}

## {.clr-5}

::: {.list-table widths="2,2,2" .small}

- - Test
  - Question
  - `lm()`

- - One-sample *t*-test
  - Is the average different from 0?
  - `lm(y ~ 1)`

- - Two-sample *t*-test
  - Are two averages different?
  - `lm(y ~ group_binary)`

- - Difference in proportions
  - Are two proportions different?
  - `lm(y_binary ~ group)`

- - ANOVA
  - Are several averages different?
  - `lm(y ~ category)`

- - Multiple regression
  - All of that ↑, holding other things constant
  - `lm(y ~ x + z + ...)`

:::

::: {.smaller}
See ["Common statistical tests are linear models"](https://lindeloev.github.io/tests-as-linear/)
:::

## Difference in means {.clr-5}

[Do democracies have higher life expectancy than autocracies?]{.box-clr-5-light}

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Simulation
vdem |> specify(life_exp ~ democracy) |> ...

# t-test
vdem |> t_test(life_exp ~ democracy, var.equal = TRUE, ...)

# Regression
lm(life_exp ~ democracy, data = vdem)
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
```{r}
tribble(
  ~Method, ~δ, ~`p-value`,
  "Simulation (1,000 shuffles)", obs_life$stat, fmt_p_cell(p_life_sim),
  "t-test", t_life$estimate, fmt_p_cell(t_life$p_value),
  "Regression", lm_life$estimate[2], fmt_p_cell(lm_life$p.value[2])
) |>
  mutate(δ = round(δ, 2)) |>
  tt_nice(size = 0.8)
```
:::

## Difference in means {.clr-5}

[Do democracies have higher turnout than autocracies?]{.box-clr-5-light}

::: {.smaller}
```{.r}
# Simulation
vdem |> specify(turnout ~ democracy) |> ...

# t-test
vdem |> t_test(turnout ~ democracy, var.equal = TRUE, ...)

# Regression
lm(turnout ~ democracy, data = vdem)
```
:::

```{r}
tribble(
  ~Method, ~δ, ~`p-value`,
  "Simulation (1,000 shuffles)", obs_turnout$stat, fmt_p_cell(p_turnout_sim),
  "t-test", t_turnout$estimate, fmt_p_cell(t_turnout$p_value),
  "Regression", lm_turnout$estimate[2], fmt_p_cell(lm_turnout$p.value[2])
) |>
  mutate(δ = round(δ, 2)) |>
  tt_nice(size = 0.8)
```

## Difference in proportions {.clr-5}

[Do women and men in Mauritania vote at different rates?]{.box-clr-5-light}

::: {.smaller}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mauritania <- mauritania |> mutate(voted_num = as.numeric(voted == "Yes"))
lm(voted_num ~ gender, data = mauritania)
```

:::

```{r}
tribble(
  ~Method, ~δ, ~`p-value`,
  "Simulation (1,000 shuffles)", obs_vote$stat, fmt_p_cell(p_vote_sim),
  "Proportion test", obs_vote$stat, fmt_p_cell(prop_vote$p_value),
  "Regression", lm_vote$estimate[2], fmt_p_cell(lm_vote$p.value[2])
) |>
```

## Holding things constant {.clr-5}

[Each coefficient in a multiple regression is its own test too]{.box-clr-5-light}

::: {.incremental .sp-before}
- $H_0$: β = 0, *holding all the other variables constant*
- A variable can be significant on its own but stop being significant once you control for other things (or the other way around!)
:::

# Reading<br>regression tables {#reading-regression-tables background-color="{{< brand color clr-7 >}}" background-image="/slides/img/background-hex-shapes.svg" background-opacity="0.25"}

## You'll see these everywhere {.clr-7}

[Do richer countries have more women in their legislatures?]{.box-clr-7-light .small}

```{r}
modelsummary(
  wl_models,
  coef_map = wl_coefs,
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared")
) |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.7) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```

## {.clr-7}

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
modelsummary(
  wl_models,
  coef_map = wl_coefs,
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared")
) |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.6) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```
::::

:::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.incremental .small}
- Each column is a different model
- Each row is a variable
- The number is β
- The number in parentheses underneath is (usually) the standard error
- Stars show the p-value
- An empty cell means that variable isn't in that model
- The bottom rows describe the whole model: number of observations, R², etc.
:::
::::

:::::

## {.clr-7}

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
modelsummary(
  wl_models,
  coef_map = wl_coefs,
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared")
) |>
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.6) |>
  style_tt(i = 1, j = c(2, 4), background = "#f7e896", bold = TRUE) |>
  theme_html(class = "tinytable shadow")
```
::::

:::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.incremental .smaller}
- **Model 1**: A \$1,000 increase in GDP per capita is associated with `r round(b_wl_1$estimate, 3)` more percentage points of women legislators, on average (p `r fmt_p(b_wl_1$p.value)`)
- **Model 3**: Holding democracy constant, that drops to `r round(b_wl_3$estimate, 3)` and isn't significant anymore (p `r fmt_p(b_wl_3$p.value)`)
- Democracy stays significant, even after holding wealth constant
- Richer countries tend to be more democratic, so model 1 was partly picking up democracy
:::
::::

:::::

## Watch out! {.clr-7}

::: {.incremental}
- The (parentheses) might be standard errors, *t* statistics, or p-values, and sometimes [brackets] are confidence intervals
- The stars aren't standard!<br>Lots of papers use `*` p < 0.1, `**` p < 0.05, `***` p < 0.01
- Always read the note at the bottom!
:::

## {.clr-7}

::: {.box-center}
[[**{modelsummary}**](https://modelsummary.com/)]{.box-clr-7-light}
:::

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(modelsummary)

model1 <- lm(women_legislators ~ gdp_1000, data = vdem)
model2 <- lm(women_legislators ~ polyarchy, data = vdem)
model3 <- lm(women_legislators ~ gdp_1000 + polyarchy, data = vdem)

modelsummary(
  list("(1)" = model1, "(2)" = model2, "(3)" = model3),
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared")
)
```
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Use `coef_rename` or `coef_map` to give the variables nicer names
:::
